paragraphs: Friend, here's what gets me about this passage. Josiah hears the Book of the Covenant, and he doesn't just feel bad about it. He reads it in the hearing of all the people, stands by the pillar, and makes a covenant before the LORD "to follow the LORD and to keep His commandments, decrees, and statutes with all his heart and all his soul" (2 Kings 23:2-3). Hearing God's Word was never meant to stop at the ears. It's meant to move your hands and your feet.

Now look at how far he goes. Altars on the roof, horses at the LORD's front door, high places from Geba to Beersheba, and he keeps going all the way to Bethel and the cities of Samaria (2 Kings 23:4-19). I have a few little habits in my own bakery that should've been cleaned out years ago, and I keep saying I'll get to them LATER. Josiah shows us that real obedience doesn't clean one corner and call it a day.

And one more thing, baker. Even in the middle of all that tearing down, Josiah sees a monument and asks about it, and when the men of the city tell him it's the tomb of the man of God, he says, "Let him rest" (2 Kings 23:17-18). That's a king who took the LORD's Word seriously, tearing down the idols and leaving the man of God's bones alone. Josiah's story isn't over yet, so keep your oven warm.
